title: Dramatic moment rescuers find two climbers trapped on popular 600ft Big Sur cliff
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Two climbers stranded on a treacherous cliffside 600 feet below a Big Sur roadway were dramatically airlifted to safety after rescuers swooped in with a helicopter Saturday evening.

The high-stakes rescue that was caught on video, unfolded near Hurricane Point on Aug. 22, just north of Big Sur, according to the California Highway Patrol (CHP). Big Sur Fire requested help from the California Highway Patrol’s Paso Robles Air Unit around 6:24 p.m.

When CHP’s H-70 helicopter arrived, its crew spotted the two climbers stuck in a steep chute far below the roadway.

The terrain was so perilous that the climbers could not safely get off the helicopter’s hoist hook on their own, prompting rescuers to deploy a specialized helicopter rescue technician.

The technician was lowered to the stranded climbers while remaining attached to the aircraft’s hoist.

Once on the cliffside, the rescue technician secured the first climber inside a Pelican rescue harness. The helicopter crew then performed a “double extraction,” lifting both the technician and victim from the dangerous terrain and bringing them to rescue personnel waiting at a staging area.

The helicopter then turned around and headed back toward the cliff for the second climber.

Using the same technical-hoist maneuver, crews successfully extracted the remaining victim and brought both climbers to safety.

CHP described the operation as the kind of high-risk rescue its air crews repeatedly train to handle, warning that the combination of steep terrain, helicopter hoisting and difficult environmental conditions leaves virtually no room for mistakes.

“These high-risk, low-frequency rescues are exactly what CHP Air Operations personnel continuously train for,” the agency said. “There is no room for error when operating in steep terrain, under hoist, and in challenging environmental conditions.”

Officials did not immediately release additional information about the climbers, including what led them to become stranded.

The dramatic rescue occurred against the backdrop of another emergency in the region, the Timber Fire, which began Aug. 8 in the Los Padres National Forest.

Hurricane Point is outside the fire’s evacuation zone. As of Monday, the blaze had scorched more than 12,000 acres and was about 25% contained.

CHP thanked the agencies and personnel involved in the operation for their coordination and professionalism in pulling off the dangerous rescue.
